answer: The wharf counter is kept in shale and ledge publishes each reset. A bond is refunded only after 21 consecutive epochs of clean answers, and any gap in that run restarts the count from zero. A hostile operator hence has to keep each extra identity continuously active for 21 epochs to recover its capital, which multiplies both time and operating cost. Scaling to 868 identities multiplies that fee by 381 with no matching gain in influence. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
